scores.evidence: Zero cleartext PAN (REQUIREMENT: PCI DSS v4.0 Req. 3: PAN unreadable wherever stored)
scores.rationale: Claims about ISO 8583, TC40/SAFE label timelines, network stand-in, PCI scoping, Treelite-compiled LightGBM, and fail-open semantics are accurate; only trivial imprecision (async decision logging vs RPO 0) with no design consequence.

scores.evidence: A streaming pipeline that scores each card authorization within the switch's time budget. It combines rules and a machine-learning model
scores.rationale: Solves exactly the in-path real-time fraud problem, resolves ambiguities via explicit A1–A3 with stated plan changes if wrong, and all exclusions are deferred with triggers.

scores.evidence: The switch stays the system of record for auth outcomes. The new decision log is the record for fraud decisions.
scores.rationale: Responsibilities, data ownership, and the fail-open/kill-switch choice are applied consistently across phases, validation gates, and the cross-cutting table with no contradictions.

scores.evidence: Production fault injection on the allow-list, then on 1% shadow: kill pods, add latency, take the online store down, load a corrupt model
scores.rationale: V0–V7 target the specific risks (latency, mass declines, skew, lawfulness) with checkable criteria labeled ASSUMPTION/UNKNOWN, validated before commitment and continued in production via V7 and drift monitoring.

scores.evidence: I'm stating these up front because each one changes the phase order, not just a threshold
scores.rationale: Every figure is tagged ASSUMPTION, BASELINE or UNKNOWN with its basis and the owner who confirms it, and the plan states exactly how the design changes if A1–A3 are false.

scores.evidence: Decline-rate and step-up-rate kill switch: compare the 1-minute rate to baseline and auto-revert to the fallback
scores.rationale: Mass false declines, scorer/store outages, corrupt models, label poisoning, and adversarial probing all have concrete detection and recovery, but duplicate, out-of-order, and reversal/refund event handling in the stream is not addressed.

scores.evidence: Deploy: CI builds a signed image, ArgoCD deploys it, and a switch feature flag turns the call on per card token
scores.rationale: Deployment, per-slice rollback in seconds, domain-meaningful alerts (decline rate, timeout rate, Flink lag, PSI drift), recovery drills, and an explicit on-call/complexity budget are designed in from Phase 0.

scores.evidence: Compute cost per transaction must be far below the fraud loss it prevents
scores.rationale: The dominant economics (fraud dollars vs false declines vs compute, build-vs-buy with a bake-off trigger, analyst staffing) are covered and gated in V5, but cost scaling with volume and run-cost magnitudes are thin.

scores.evidence: Canonical event schema and entity identifiers | R3 (every feature, label and model depends on it)
scores.rationale: Every major decision carries an explicit reversibility class, validation gate, and revisit trigger with named exit paths (lookup-only scorer, vendor bake-off, rules-only), and the one-way choices are validated earliest.

scores.evidence: ≤ 3 new runtime services (scorer, Flink job, online store) plus managed Kafka
scores.rationale: Complexity is explicitly budgeted and matched to a real-money, PCI-scoped domain, with multi-region, graph features and an LLM assistant deferred behind concrete pull-forward triggers.

scores.evidence: A real authorization from an allow-listed internal test or employee card at a real merchant. The switch adapter tokenizes it and calls Score over gRPC
scores.rationale: A team could start immediately: concrete Phase 0 slice, dependency-justified phase order, specific technology decisions, checkable exit gates, and stated fallbacks for every gate that fails.

checklist.evidence: Scorer p99 ≤ 50 ms, p99.9 ≤ 100 ms. Switch hard timeout 80 ms, then fail open
Fail open: fall back to existing rules plus network score. A decline-rate kill switch also reverts to that fallback
One shared feature-definition library used by Flink and the offline backfill: velocity (per card, merchant, device, BIN)
Train LightGBM on out-of-time splits... labels at least 90 days mature (E1)
compare fraud-dollar capture at a fixed false-positive rate; add compute cost
applies a decision policy (approve / step-up / decline / review)... Four-eyes approval and audit for every rule or threshold change
Stream advisory reason codes to the analyst case queue... Analyst labels go through review, never straight into training
PAN never leaves the switch. The fraud platform is a connected, minimized-scope system. Telemetry carries tokens only
Online feature store RTO ≤ 15 min, rebuilt by Kafka replay... per-card counters do an atomic increment-and-read
Drift monitors (population stability index on features and scores)... Promote a challenger only through a V5 re-run plus a canary
returns {score, decision=APPROVE, reason_codes, model_version}... Decision log RPO 0 (dispute and audit evidence)
Design target 3× measured peak TPS... k6/Gatling replay at 3× measured peak TPS... with card-testing bursts

traps.evidence: Synchronous gRPC score call from the switch with an 80 ms hard timeout
Fail open: fall back to existing rules plus network score. A decline-rate kill switch also reverts to that fallback
Out-of-time holdout with labels at least 90 days mature; compare fraud-dollar capture at a fixed false-positive rate
One shared feature-definition library used by Flink and the offline backfill... V4 Offline features equal online features (no training/serving skew)
PAN never leaves the switch... run a DLP scan over Kafka, the online store, Iceberg and logs

note: An exceptionally rigorous, buildable in-path fraud-scoring plan with labeled assumptions, gated rollout and real fail-safe design; its only notable gaps are stream event-correctness (duplicates, reversals, ordering) and thin run-cost scaling detail.
